children: The unemployment rate in the Philippines fell to 5.3% in August 2026 from a four-year high of 6% in the previous month.

The number of unemployed persons declined to 2.77 million from 3.14 million, while the employment rate rose to 94.7% from 94% and the number of employed persons increased to 49.79 million from 49.21 million over the same period.
The underemployment rate also eased to 11.9% from 12.9%, with 5.90 million workers seeking additional hours or another job.
On a year-on-year basis, however, the unemployment rate remained above 3.9% in August 2025, while the employment rate was below 96.1% and the number of employed persons was down from 50.10 million.
The underemployment rate was also higher than 10.7% a year earlier.
The services sector remained the largest employer, accounting for 61.7% of total employment, followed by agriculture at 20.9% and industry at 17.3%.
Average weekly working hours fell to 39.2 from 40.6 in July and 41.0 a year earlier.

title: Philippines Jobless Rate Falls to 5.3%
